claim.why_it_matters: The whole left column loses its sub-entry indentation, so sub-entries read as top-level index terms. Informative index only.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (printed 917) shows a two-level index. In the left column, sub-entries are visibly indented under their head terms: Category names and Field names under Locale; SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 231 under LOCALE clause; PICTURE clause, SET statement and SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 232 under LOCALE phrase; Definition, OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph, Scope of, SET statement and SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 231 under Locale-name; FILE-CONTROL paragraph under LOCK MODE clause; the four statements under LOCK phrase; and so on. The markdown gives every left-column line the same 3-space prefix with no   marker. After the M heading the markdown uses   for sub-entries, so its own convention marks hierarchy and the left column drops it. The result is that sub-entries such as 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 231' and 'Definition 80' read as top-level index terms, which changes what the index says. The quoted text in both sources is accurate. This is not normative: it affects the informative index only.
